output.summary: A herbaceous perennial native to Eurasia and temperate Africa, greater plantain forms a broad leaf rosette and narrow flower spikes bearing many small, bitter seeds. Young tender leaves are eaten in salads, older leaves can be stewed, and the seeds can be ground as a flour substitute or extender.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves are eaten raw; older leaves are cooked in stews. The tiny seeds can be ground as a flour substitute or extender.
